name: NASA International Space Apps Challenge
organizer: NASA Space Apps Global Organizing Team
venue: In-person and virtual Local Events worldwide, plus the virtual Universal Event

timeline.what: Challenge summaries published; team formation opens
Full challenge statements with data sets and requirements
Project Submission and Judging & Awards guides published
Hackathon starts; project submission opens 09:00 local time
December 2026: Global Nominees, Finalists and Honorable Mentions announced

criteria.label: Impact
criteria.description: Carried from 2025 until the 2026 Judging & Awards guide is published (2026-11-13).

judging.judge_profile_summary: Expected three phases as in 2025: Local/Universal Event judges → NASA and Space Agency Partner subject-matter experts → an executive committee of agency leaders.
judging.notes: Criteria and award list are provisional until 2026-11-13. Recognition for 2026 Global Winners is 'to be announced'.

required_tech: At least one NASA data source or resource (expected, as in 2025)
submission_requirements: Teams of at most six, all registered for the same Local Event or the Universal Event
Teams must not begin working on the challenges before the hackathon
Submit through the team's project page on spaceappschallenge.org by the end of the Local Event

guide.summary: A 48-hour hackathon on NASA data, run at hundreds of Local Events and a virtual Universal Event. Global awards pass three judging phases, so the submitted project page has to carry the project after your Local Event.
guide.before_the_event: Register, join a Local Event or the Universal Event, form a team of up to six, and study NASA data portals and past winners. The rules forbid starting on the 2026 challenges before the hackathon.

rules.rule: Teams must not begin working on the challenges before the hackathon.
rules.effect: Before November 14, study problem families, data sources and past winners; no solution design or code for a challenge.

rules.rule: Full challenge statements, with data and requirements, arrive on October 28.
rules.effect: Map your problem families to the published challenges then, and drop the families with no match.

rules.rule: Criteria and the award list stay provisional until the Judging & Awards guide on November 13.
rules.effect: Re-read the rubric that day; write or revise the demo script only after the hackathon starts.

rules.rule: Submission closes at 23:59 local time on November 15, through the team project page.
rules.effect: Write-up, demo video and repository are what later judging phases see; budget hours for them.

rules.rule: In 2025, projects had to use and link at least one NASA data source, disclose every AI tool and avoid NASA branding.
rules.effect: Expect the same in 2026: pick the dataset early and test access on day one.

rules.rule: In 2025, Local Awards were separate and did not qualify a team for global judging.
rules.effect: Aim the submission at the global criteria, not only at the room you present in.

ask_organizers: Does your Local Event run its own judging and awards, and when do teams present?
What are the venue hours, and can teams work overnight?
guide.evidence_note: These priors come from 20 winners of the 2024 and 2025 editions. A pre-registered backtest on the 2024 winners (docs/research/holdout-nasa-2024.md) found them only partly predictive: the agency playbook beat chance mainly through expert data made usable for everyone, which the challenges themselves ask for. Use them to check an idea, not to choose one.
guide.harness_note: Run recon and patterns fully, and angles only as problem families and angle shapes. Everything from the judge gate on waits until November 14. The repository keeps a worked example in hack-plan/nasa-space-apps-2026/.

sources.note: Dates, theme, timeline, team rules, no work before the hackathon.

curator_notes: Dogfood target for the /hack-plan harness (hack-plan/nasa-space-apps-2026/). Prior: nasa-space-apps-2025.
